name: JSNS2-II
full_name: J-PARC Sterile Neutrino Search, second-baseline extension
summary: JSNS2-II adds a farther liquid-scintillator detector to JSNS2 so that a possible appearance signal can be tested through its baseline dependence. The farther apparatus was completed and being commissioned in May 2026.
physics_targets: Baseline-dependent test of the LSND anomaly
detection_principle: The far detector uses the same prompt-positron and delayed-gadolinium-capture inverse-beta signature as JSNS2. Comparing two baselines helps separate an oscillatory signal from source normalization and detector backgrounds.

status.label: Commissioning
status.evidence: The dated May 2026 collaboration contribution states the far detector is complete and currently being commissioned.

timeline.event: J-PARC newsletter described preparation of the two-detector programme
Completed far detector undergoing calibration and commissioning

collaboration.name: JSNS2-II Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Far baseline
key_parameters.value: 48 m from the J-PARC MLF mercury target

key_parameters.name: Detection channel
key_parameters.value: Inverse beta decay with delayed gadolinium neutron capture

key_parameters.name: Relationship
key_parameters.value: Second-baseline extension of JSNS2, not an independent neutrino source

results.summary: Commissioning report documents scintillator conditioning, liquid-level stabilization and trigger development. It does not establish a final oscillation result.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
